sign.name: Mise en abyme
sign.operation: Frame the singer with a tableau of the horse behind him in the lamplight while Odysseus listens in the foreground; the told Troy and the listening hall share the image.

scenes.world: The same lamplit banquet hall at night, deep shadows and flickering oil lamps, silent costume-drama staging.

captain.asks: Frame the singer with a tableau of the horse behind him while Odysseus weeps in the foreground, so sung Troy and the listening hall share one lamplit image.
diagnosis: The two layers never coexist: Troy (fire, gate) and the hall (tuxedo tables) alternate as separate films, no tableau holds both.
The weeping, the scene's hinge, is played by a melodrama heroine in a forest and a fallen white shape; the man never appears.
Night-black and lamp-glow hold a shared palette, which keeps a stranger in one mood if not one place.
